pattern-selector.why: the forces are one unsatisfiable-key footgun at a gate's CLI boundary; the fit is a single guard clause clustered with the sibling arg guards, deliberately no new abstraction (no factory/strategy for one check).
pattern-selector.what: added an anchored SHA-shape reject beside the existing --change / --changed-list guards; recorded the options and the rejected fuzzy-resolve option in ADR-0114.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: keying the review gate on a stable ref rather than a SHA is a lasting contract decision; a future maintainer will ask why a SHA is rejected and why the branch is the key.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0114 (root cause, options, the rejected fuzzy-resolve, consequences, limits).
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the gate's behavior changed (a SHA-shaped change now fails with a named diagnostic, a branch passes), so the use cases are enumerated as Gherkin for the agent and operator audiences and logged.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added an executable feature (SHA rejected 40/64-hex, branch passes, no SHA-keyed entry in the repo) with a steps file that spawns the real gate, plus an append-only coverage-log entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the defect is a CLI-contract behavior, so the test spawns the real gate end to end against faithful log fixtures and scans the real repo, not a unit test of an extracted predicate.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added five node:test cases that run check-arch-review-coverage.mjs and a real-repo invariant scanning docs/arch-reviews/entries.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the fix must fail when the guard is neutralized; because the no-match path also exits 1, the tests assert the diagnostic message, not just the exit code.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: mutation pass: no-opped the SHA guard and confirmed the two SHA tests go red (lose the 'commit SHA' message); restored the guard; recorded the proof in the review entry.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the claim that #204 and #203 were still open was a claim to disconfirm, not assume: each was checked against the current tree (ADR-0109, routing, the real-repo integrity test) before being called resolved.
skeptical-audit.what: recorded the disconfirming pass and the honest limits of the #213 fix (full-length SHAs only; non-SHA arbitrary keys still a judgment call) in ADR-0114.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the change edits a gate script, so it got a fresh-context four-question review over every changed code file, with the grep battery run.
judge-arch.what: a fresh-context subagent reviewed both code files (PASS, 1 low error-handling finding in the invariant test); the finding was fixed and the review recorded.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the simplest thing that meets the requirement (a SHA can never match) is one anchored guard plus doc and recipe fixes, not a history-resolving key or a new matching layer.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept the change to one guard clause, the contract text, and a committed consumer recipe; rejected fuzzy SHA-to-branch resolution as added coupling.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, retention, or migration; the review log's append-only/tamper-evident property is unchanged (only the key's shape is constrained).

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no untrusted input, auth, session, secret, file, or network surface; the added regexes are anchored fixed-length (^[0-9a-f]{40}$ / {64}$) with no quantifier nesting, so no ReDoS, and --change is matched by equality, never interpolated into a shell or query.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature flag, or service rollout; the change ships to consumers as a gate-script and doc update, with the correct wiring recipe documented.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert; a build-time CI gate.

arch-encode.why: the caught mistake is encoded as a fail-closed guard in the gate itself plus a real-repo invariant test, not as an arch-gate grep rule, because it is a CLI-contract shape the gate owns, not a source pattern arch-gate scans.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; a Node CLI gate.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the gate's diagnostic names the problem, why a SHA can never match, and the fix (key on the branch/PR ref) in plain words.
